items.followUp: How many significant figures are in the measurement 0.0450 m?

rubric.why: A significant-figure definition must identify the reliably known digits and the final estimated digit.
rubric.description: Defines significant figures as the reliably known digits plus one estimated digit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both the known/reliable digits and the estimated/uncertain digit are included.

rubric.why: The answer must give an example and correctly identify its significant figures.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as 12.3 cm, and states the number of significant figures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid measurement example with its correct significant-figure count.

modelAnswer: Significant figures are the reliably known digits in a measurement plus the first estimated digit.
For example, 12.3 cm has 3 significant figures.

items.followUp: Differentiate between circular motion and oscillatory motion.

rubric.why: Random motion is distinguished by its irregular, unpredictable path or direction.
rubric.description: States that random motion has an irregular or unpredictable path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying random motion as irregular or unpredictable.

rubric.why: Linear motion is distinguished by motion along a straight line.
rubric.description: States that linear motion is along a straight line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying linear motion as motion along a straight path.

modelAnswer: In random motion, a body moves irregularly in an unpredictable direction or path.
In linear motion, a body moves along a straight line.

items.followUp: Can a body moving with constant speed in a circular path have acceleration? Explain why.

rubric.why: The answer must recognize that constant speed does not rule out acceleration.
rubric.description: Answers yes: a body moving at constant speed can have acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear affirmative answer.

rubric.why: Acceleration occurs because velocity changes when its direction changes, even if speed stays constant.
rubric.description: Explains that a change in direction changes velocity and produces acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the change in direction to a change in velocity or acceleration.

modelAnswer: Yes. A body moving at constant speed can have acceleration if its direction changes.
In circular motion, the direction of velocity changes continuously, so the body is accelerated.

items.followUp: Why do action and reaction forces not cancel each other?

rubric.why: Action and reaction act on separate bodies, which is the key reason they do not cancel on one body.
rubric.description: States that action and reaction act on different bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that the forces act on different bodies or objects.

rubric.why: Since the forces do not cancel on the same body, a body's motion depends on the resultant force acting on it.
rubric.description: Explains that the forces do not cancel on one body and motion depends on the net force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the pair does not cancel on a single body, or that the body's motion depends on its net force.

modelAnswer: Action and reaction act on different bodies, so they do not cancel each other on one body.
A body moves or changes its motion when the resultant force acting on it is not zero.

items.followUp: Define momentum and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Momentum is defined as the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Defines momentum as the product of a body's mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The formula is the requested mathematical expression for momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass and velocity of a body.

items.followUp: State the direction of the centripetal force on a body moving in a circular path and contrast it with centrifugal force.

rubric.why: Centripetal force acts radially inward, toward the centre of the circular path.
rubric.description: States that centripetal force is directed toward the centre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct inward direction.

rubric.why: Centrifugal force is described as directed away from the centre, opposite to centripetal force.
rubric.description: States that centrifugal force is directed away from the centre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct outward direction.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force acts toward the centre of the circular path.
Centrifugal force acts away from the centre, opposite to centripetal force.

items.followUp: Define stable equilibrium and give one example.

rubric.why: In neutral equilibrium, a slight displacement leaves the body in its new position; its centre of gravity remains at the same height.
rubric.description: Defines neutral equilibrium by the body's remaining in its new position after a slight displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition, ideally noting that the centre-of-gravity height is unchanged.

rubric.why: A ball on a horizontal surface is a standard example of neutral equilibrium.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as a ball on a horizontal surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example.

modelAnswer: A body is in neutral equilibrium if, after a slight displacement, it remains in its new position; the height of its centre of gravity remains unchanged.
Example: a ball resting on a horizontal surface.

items.followUp: Find the horizontal component of a 40 N force making an angle of 60° with the X-axis.

rubric.why: The vertical component is obtained using F sin θ when the angle is measured from the X-axis.
rubric.description: Chooses the correct component formula, Fᵧ = F sin θ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Substitution and evaluation give 50 sin 30° = 25 N.
rubric.description: Substitutes the given values and obtains 25 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct calculation and answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 50 N, θ = 30° (in SI units).
Answer: The vertical component of the force is 25 N.
